result.plan_summary:
I read every in-scope module against the current tree (HEAD 2e41128). All three seed findings are real. I also found six more reproducible defects. I checked each by reading the code, and for decide I also ran a probe. The nine items, highest value first:

- **Synthesis: tools that silently misbehave or never appear.** The resolver ignores `data-test`. Fill appends to whatever is already in the field instead of replacing it. Form-less search boxes never become tools. The fingerprint depends on scroll position, so the cache and the verified flag are lost on large pages.
- **WebMCP: stale synthesized tool beats the page's own.** `call_tool` can run an old synthesized tool when the page now declares a tool with the same name. That breaks the "declared always wins" rule.
- **Human input: stuck keys and buttons.** If a step is cancelled mid-gesture, keys and the mouse button stay pressed.
- **Cobrowse: leaked Chrome process.** If launch fails, the Chrome process is left running, and the profile lock with it.
- **Decide: breaks its never-raises promise.** `ask()` crashes on a malformed `usage` block. `choose_tool` can also return a tool it never offered.
- **Bridge: two problems, `bridge.py` only.** Discovery can hang on a stalled manifest fetch. The bridge also installs `window.agent`, which its own comment says it deliberately does not do.
- **Profile (lowest priority).** In headless mode on macOS and Windows, the user agent claims Linux.

**How the work splits.** Every item touches its own set of source files except FIX-1 and FIX-2. Both edit `browser_use/synthesis/service.py`, but in separate places (FIX-1: `RESOLVE_JS` and `call()`; FIX-2: `synthesize()` plus a new method). Git should merge them cleanly; merge FIX-1 first. FIX-3 alone owns `scanner.py` and `store.py`, including the single `SYNTHESIS_VERSION` bump that covers the FIX-1 and FIX-2 changes too.

**Test files.** Each item writes its regression tests in its own new file under `tests/ci/`, so parallel worktrees never conflict on the same test file. The lead can fold them into the existing test files after merging.

**Rules for every worker.** Tabs for indentation. Real browser with `pytest-httpserver`, no mocks except the LLM, no remote URLs. Confirm the test fails before the fix and passes after. Run the whole existing test file for the module touched; no existing test may be skipped or weakened.

**Left out on purpose.** I noted one more likely bug and kept it out as lower value and harder to reproduce: in `vision/live.py`, if `startScreencast` fails, `start()` leaves its frame handler registered. The next `start()` then treats its own handler as the previous one and forwards frames to itself in a loop. The lead can queue it as a follow-up.

work_items.title: Synthesis execution: resolve data-test locators, and make fill replace the field's value instead of appending
work_items.problem: (a) scanner.py:113 locatorFor records testid from `data-testid || data-test-id || data-test`, and when a testid exists it never computes a CSS fallback (scanner.py:116). But RESOLVE_JS at service.py:139-140 only queries `[data-testid=…]` and `[data-test-id=…]`. So an element carrying only `data-test` with no id and no accessible name resolves to {found:false}. Example: an unlabeled `<input data-test="city">` inside a form. call() then returns 'step N (fill) could not find [data-testid=city]' on every run, and the tool can never be verified. (b) call() at service.py:607-608 runs `human.click_box(rect)` and then `human.type_text(value)` with no clear or select step. On any field that already holds text, the new value is inserted at a random caret position (click_box aims at a jittered landing_point), not written over the old one. Typical cases: a search box on a results page pre-filled with the last query, a profile form, a second call to the same tool. search(query='new') on an input with value='old' submits something like 'oldnew' or 'olnewd'. It still reports ok=True and marks the tool verified (service.py:611).
work_items.approach: (a) In RESOLVE_JS, extend the testid chain to also try `deepQuery(`[data-test="${CSS.escape(loc.testid)}"]`)[0]`, keeping the same order as locatorFor: data-testid, then data-test-id, then data-test. Keep the scanner/resolver-parity comment accurate. (b) Before typing in a 'fill' step, select the field's current contents so the trusted keystrokes replace them. Add a resolver variant via the existing `_variant()` / `_fill()` machinery, e.g. SELECT_CONTENTS_JS: for input/textarea call `el.focus(); el.select()`; for contenteditable, select the node's contents with a Range; return {found:true}. Call it after click_box and before type_text. Page-derived data must still go through _encode/_fill only; the single-pass injection guarantee stays. Do not change behaviour when value is None or '' (the step is still skipped). Keep 'select' steps on the existing SELECT_JS path.

work_items.title: Scroll-independent fingerprint, covering form-less controls, plus the single SYNTHESIS_VERSION bump

It restores document order afterwards, which keeps names stable but not the set. fingerprint() (store.py:41-61) hashes the names of the surviving items, so on any page where a cap binds, the fingerprint depends on scroll position. synthesize() computes `shape = fingerprint(affordances)` (service.py:474) and serves the in-memory or on-disk manifest only when it matches exactly (service.py:476-482, store.py:140). Separately, fingerprint() ignores `controls` entirely (store.py:49-58), so a renamed form-less search box, which FIX-2 turns into a tool, would never invalidate a cached locator.

That means the names of buttonCandidates, looseCandidates and each form's visible CONTROL_SELECTOR candidates, in document order, still bounded by the existing slice(0,200)/slice(0,120) limits so the payload stays small. work_items.title: WebMCP call_tool runs a stale synthesized tool instead of the page's own declared tool
work_items.problem: discover() only synthesizes when the page declares nothing (service.py:138), and the module promises that 'A real declaration is a contract and always wins'. call_tool() instead checks the synthesizer first (service.py:247-257). It looks up `self.synthesizer.cached(self._origin_of(target))`, which is the per-origin SiteManifest held in SiteToolSynthesizer._manifests. It then runs any synthesized tool whose name matches, without checking whether the current discovery for this target still lists that tool as synthesized. Failing sequence, with enable_webmcp=True: the page loads with a search form and no declared tools, so discovery synthesizes 'search' and the origin manifest is cached. The SPA then registers navigator.modelContext.registerTool({name:'search',…}), or the tab navigates to another page on the same origin that declares 'search'. The next discovery lists the declared js tool. call_tool('search') still runs the stale synthesized UI steps (click/type through the old form locator) instead of the site's execute() handler. The result is wrong, or it fails with 'could not find'.
work_items.approach: In call_tool, take the synthesized path only when the latest discovery for this target lists the tool as synthesized: `listed = self._cache.get(cdp_session.target_id)`, `entry = listed.get(name) if listed else None`, and proceed only when `entry is not None and entry.source == 'synthesized'`. Otherwise fall through to the bridge call. Keep the existing error/ok mapping and the verified update. Pass the resolved cdp_session.target_id to synthesizer.call for consistency. Do not change discover() semantics.
work_items.acceptance: A new test fails before the fix and passes after, using a bridge-enabled session (BrowserProfile(enable_webmcp=True), as the existing webmcp_session fixture in test_site_synthesis.py does). A page has a search form and registers a declared 'search' tool via navigator.modelContext.registerTool about 1s after load, whose execute returns 'declared:'+q. Discover once (synthesized 'search' appears). Wait until the declared tool exists, discover again (declared 'search' is listed with source 'js'), then call_tool('search', {'q':'x'}). The result content is 'declared:x', and the form was not submitted. tests/ci/test_webmcp.py and test_site_synthesis.py still pass, including test_what_the_site_declares_always_wins and test_calling_a_synthesized_tool_really_drives_the_page.
work_items.test_idea: Serve the page with pytest-httpserver. Make the form's onsubmit set window.__formUsed=true so the test can assert the synthesized path did not run. Use browser_session.get_webmcp_tools() for discovery and the webmcp service's call_tool (or the session helper that wraps it) for the call.

work_items.title: Human input: a cancelled hold, press_and_hold, click or keystroke leaves the key or mouse button stuck down
work_items.problem: hold() (input.py:247-263) sends keyDown, loops sending autoRepeat keyDowns until the deadline, then sends keyUp, with no try/finally. press_and_hold() (input.py:277-279) sends mousePressed, sleeps for `seconds`, then sends mouseReleased. click() (input.py:135-137), press() (input.py:210-218) and type_text() (input.py:180-189) all have an awaited sleep between the down and up events. Agent steps run under timeouts; live.py's watch() documents 'A step timeout cancels us mid-sleep'. If the task is cancelled during any of those sleeps, the release event is never dispatched. The page and Blink's input state keep the key held or the left button pressed: games keep accelerating, and later mouseMoved events are seen as a drag with the button held. This lasts until some later input happens to send the matching up event.
work_items.approach: Wrap every down…up pair in try/finally so the release is always dispatched: keyUp in hold/press/type_text, mouseReleased in click/press_and_hold. In the finally block, send the release with the same params (the existing `up` dict / button / clickCount at the current coordinates). Protect it so a second cancellation or a dead session cannot mask the original exception: wrap the send in try/except Exception and log via logger.debug; asyncio.shield around the dispatch is optional. Re-raise CancelledError as usual, never swallow it. Keep tabs and existing timing and jitter behaviour unchanged.
work_items.acceptance: New tests fail before the fix and pass after. (1) Start `asyncio.create_task(browser_session.human.hold('ArrowRight', 5))` on a page that logs keydown/keyup into window.__log, cancel it after about 0.4s, await it expecting CancelledError. The last logged ArrowRight event is 'keyup'. (2) Same pattern with press_and_hold over a box on a page logging mousedown/mouseup: after cancellation the last event is 'mouseup'. tests/ci/test_human_input.py still passes.

work_items.title: Cobrowse: launch_for_human leaks the Chrome process (and its profile lock) when the debugging port never comes up
work_items.problem: launch_for_human() starts Chrome with asyncio.create_subprocess_exec (service.py:165) and then awaits `_wait_for_cdp(port, process)` (service.py:167) with no try/except. When _wait_for_cdp raises TimeoutError after LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_S=30s, or any other exception such as CancelledError from a caller timeout or a bad /json/version body raising KeyError, the process is never terminated and nothing holds a reference to it. Chrome keeps running with the persistent profile locked, so the next launch against the same profile, the whole point of cobrowse, fails or attaches to the orphan. HumanBrowser.close() also calls process.kill() after the terminate timeout (service.py:94-95) without awaiting process.wait(), which leaves a zombie. And terminate() can raise ProcessLookupError if the process exits in between.
work_items.approach: Wrap the _wait_for_cdp call so that on any BaseException the just-started process is terminated, then killed if it has not exited within a few seconds, and then awaited (reaped), before re-raising. Put this in a small `_terminate(process)` helper and reuse it in HumanBrowser.close()'s signal fallback, guarding ProcessLookupError and awaiting wait() after kill. For testability, add an optional `launch_timeout: float = LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_S` parameter to launch_for_human and thread it into _wait_for_cdp (which gains a timeout argument). The default behaviour stays the same. Leave cdp_url_for and attach unchanged.
work_items.acceptance: A new test fails before the fix and passes after. Write an executable shell script into tmp_path that ignores its arguments and sleeps: `#!/bin/sh\nexec sleep 30`. Call launch_for_human(user_data_dir=tmp_path/'p', executable_path=str(script), headless=True, launch_timeout=1.5) and expect a TimeoutError. Afterwards no child process of the test process is still running (psutil.Process().children(recursive=True) is empty of 'sleep', allowing a brief wait). Existing tests/ci/test_cobrowse.py passes.
work_items.test_idea: Use psutil, already a dependency, to list children before and after. No mocking: the fake 'browser' is a real executable that simply never opens the port.

work_items.title: Decide: parse_decisions raises on a malformed usage block (breaks the never-raises contract), and choose_tool can return a tool it never offered
work_items.problem: The module contract (service.py:3-6, ask() docstring 'Never raises') says every failure path returns an empty result. But parse_decisions runs outside ask()'s try block (service.py:95), and service.py:125-126 does `int(usage.get('input_tokens') or 0)`. I probed this: a body with usage {'input_tokens': 'n/a'} raises ValueError, {'input_tokens': inf} raises OverflowError, and {'input_tokens': [1]} raises TypeError, all of which propagate out of Jev.ask() into the agent step. Separately, choose_tool (page.py:235-241) returns any Choice answer that is not NO_TOOL and passes certain(). It never checks that answer.value is one of the offered option names, even though views.py says answers are 'validated on the way in'. A response picking 'delete_account' or a hallucinated name with confidence 0.95 is returned as the tool to call.
work_items.approach: In parse_decisions, coerce the token counts through a small `_count(value) -> int` helper that returns 0 for anything that is not a finite non-negative int/float, and excludes bool. As defence in depth, also wrap the parse_decisions call in ask() so any unexpected parse error logs at debug and returns Decisions(). Keep ValueError for more than MAX_QUESTIONS questions, which is a deliberate caller error covered by an existing test. Drop non-finite probabilities and confidence values (math.isfinite). In choose_tool, return None when `answer.value not in options` (the dict that was actually sent), logging via logger.debug.
work_items.acceptance: New tests fail before the fix and pass after. (1) With the jev_server-style pytest-httpserver endpoint returning {'answers':{}, 'usage':{'input_tokens':'n/a','output_tokens':1e400}}, `await Jev(api_key='k', url=server_url).ask(state, {...})` returns an empty or valid Decisions without raising. (2) An endpoint answering the 'tool' choice with 'not_offered' at confidence 0.99 makes choose_tool return None. All of tests/ci/test_decide.py still passes, including test_too_many_questions_is_an_error_not_a_silent_truncation.
work_items.test_idea: Copy the jev_server fixture pattern from tests/ci/test_decide.py (pytest-httpserver responding with JSON). Build page_tools as a WebMCPPageTools with two WebMCPTool entries for choose_tool.

work_items.title: WebMCP bridge: the manifest deadline does not bound in-flight fetches (discovery can hang indefinitely), and window.agent is installed despite the stated policy
work_items.problem: (a) LIMITS.manifestMs (bridge.py:34-38) is documented as 'a deadline for the whole loading pass', but loadManifests only checks it between refs (bridge.py:191). The manifest fetch at bridge.py:202 has no AbortSignal, and the tools/list rpc at bridge.py:220 uses the full 30s rpcMs. A manifest URL that accepts the connection and never responds leaves the single shared inFlightDiscovery promise (bridge.py:278-281) pending forever. Every later discover() returns that same stuck promise, so Python times out each agent step and serves stale or empty tools. bridge.call() for any name missing from manifestTools awaits bridge.discover() (bridge.py:328-330), so it hangs until the Python 30s call timeout. (b) bridge.py:370-373 says 'Deliberately no window.agent alias: it is not part of any draft, so it is a free fingerprint for anti-bot scripts', yet bridge.py:375 installs `window.agent` anyway. Every bridge-enabled page therefore sees a non-standard global.
work_items.approach: (a) Create one AbortController per loadManifests pass and abort it at the deadline: setTimeout(controller.abort, LIMITS.manifestMs), cleared in a finally. Pass its signal to the manifest fetch and the res.json() read. Let rpc() accept an optional outer signal (or a remaining-time budget) so the tools/list call during loading is also bounded by the pass deadline, while tools/call keeps its own rpcMs. On abort, push 'manifest loading timed out' into errors and return what was found, so the discovery promise always settles within roughly manifestMs. (b) Delete the `install(window, 'agent', …)` line, keeping navigator.modelContext and window.modelContext, and keep the comment accurate.
work_items.acceptance: New tests fail before the fix and pass after, on a session with BrowserProfile(enable_webmcp=True). (1) A page with a JS-registered tool 'ping' and a `<link rel=model-context href=/hang>` whose handler sleeps about 12s: call_tool('missing_tool') returns ok=False with a 'no WebMCP tool named' error within about 8s, instead of timing out at 30s. After manifestMs, a fresh get_webmcp_tools() lists 'ping'. (2) On a bridge-enabled page, `typeof window.agent` evaluates to 'undefined' while navigator.modelContext is present. The existing tests/ci/test_webmcp.py passes, including test_a_page_cannot_stack_a_manifest_fetch_per_agent_step, and so does tests/ci/test_browser_fingerprint.py.
work_items.test_idea: Use a pytest-httpserver respond_with_handler that time.sleep()s to simulate the hanging manifest; construct the HTTPServer with threaded=True if the installed pytest-httpserver supports it, so the page HTML is still served. Measure elapsed time with time.monotonic() around the call. Use the webmcp_session fixture pattern from test_site_synthesis.py, or a module-local BrowserSession(browser_profile=BrowserProfile(headless=True, enable_webmcp=True, user_data_dir=None)).

work_items.title: Profile (lower priority): the headless 'headful' user agent always claims Linux, contradicting navigator.platform on macOS/Windows
work_items.problem: _headful_user_agent (profile.py:990-1010) exists to remove the automation signal, and its docstring says 'a mismatch between the UA string and the engine's real behaviour is itself a signal'. It hardcodes the OS token as 'Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) …' regardless of the host. get_args() injects it for every headless launch without a user-set UA (profile.py:1044). So every headless session on macOS or Windows sends a Linux UA while navigator.platform, userAgentData.platform and font and GPU fingerprints say MacIntel or Win32. The result is a contradiction detectable in one line of JS, which is worse than the HeadlessChrome token it replaced.
work_items.approach: Extract a pure helper, e.g. `def _ua_os_token(system: str) -> str`, mapping platform.system() values to Chrome's reduced-UA tokens: 'Darwin' → 'Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7', 'Windows' → 'Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64', anything else → 'X11; Linux x86_64'. Use it in _headful_user_agent with platform.system(). Do not change version detection or when the flag is emitted. Keep the fix to this defect only.
work_items.acceptance: A new unit test fails before the fix (the helper does not exist or does not map Darwin/Windows) and passes after: _ua_os_token('Darwin') contains 'Macintosh', _ua_os_token('Windows') contains 'Windows NT 10.0', and _ua_os_token('Linux') == 'X11; Linux x86_64'. On the Linux CI host, BrowserProfile(headless=True, user_data_dir=tmp).get_args() still contains a --user-agent= flag with 'X11; Linux x86_64' and no 'HeadlessChrome'. tests/ci/test_profile_args.py and tests/ci/test_browser_fingerprint.py pass.
work_items.test_idea: Pure-function test of the helper with explicit system strings, so there is no monkeypatching of platform, plus one get_args() assertion on the real host.

RESOLVE_JS at service.py:139-140 only queries `[data-testid=…]` and `[data-test-id=…]`. So an element that carries only `data-test` (no id, no accessible name) resolves to {found:false}, and its tool fails with 'could not find' on every call and can never be verified. (b) call() at service.py:607-608 runs human.click_box(rect) then human.type_text(value) without clearing or selecting what is already in the field. On a pre-filled field, the value is inserted at a jittered caret position, e.g. 'oldnew' or 'olnewd'. The call still reports ok=True and marks the tool verified.
work_items.approach: (a) In RESOLVE_JS, extend the testid chain with `deepQuery(`[data-test="${CSS.escape(loc.testid)}"]`)[0]`, in the same order as locatorFor, and keep the scanner/resolver parity comment accurate. (b) Add a SELECT_CONTENTS_JS resolver variant through the existing _variant()/_fill() machinery. For input/textarea it runs el.focus(); el.select(). For contenteditable it selects the node's contents with a Range. Call it after click_box and before type_text in 'fill' steps, so the trusted keystrokes replace the old contents. Page data must still pass only through _encode/_fill, so the single-pass injection guarantee holds. Steps with value None or '' are still skipped. 'select' steps stay on SELECT_JS.
work_items.acceptance: Two new tests, each failing before the fix and passing after: (1) a form whose only text input is `<input data-test="city">` delivers the called value; (2) a search input pre-filled with value="old", called with query='new', holds exactly 'new' at submit. All of tests/ci/test_site_synthesis.py still passes, including the injection tests and test_the_resolver_names_elements_the_same_way_the_scanner_does. pyright and ruff are clean.

The form either submits via GET to /done (check the query string in the request log), or its onsubmit stores input.value in window.__submitted and calls preventDefault; read that back with browser_session.run_page_script. Get tools with SiteToolSynthesizer(browser_session).synthesize() and run them with .call(tool, {...}).

work_items.title: Synthesis: turn a form-less search box into a search tool (scanner 'controls' are never used)
work_items.problem: scanner.py collects visible controls outside any form ('a site-wide search box usually lives here') and returns them as `controls`. SiteToolSynthesizer.synthesize() never reads affordances['controls'], even though ToolStep.key exists precisely for pressing Enter in a search box outside a form. A standalone `<input type=search>` with a JS keydown handler, the normal SPA search box, therefore never becomes a tool.
work_items.approach: Add a `_tool_from_control(control, used)` method and a loop over `affordances.get('controls') or []` in synthesize(), placed after the forms loop and under the MAX_TOOLS_PER_SITE guard. Accept only non-sensitive text-entry controls (textbox/searchbox, or combobox without options) that look like search: _SEARCH_HINTS in the name, role searchbox, type search, or identifier 'q'. Move that search test into a helper shared with _tool_from_form so the two cannot drift. Each tool is named self._unique('search', used), takes a required string 'query', and runs steps [fill(locator, param='query'), press(locator, key='Enter')]. Skip checkboxes, radios, buttons, selects, sensitive fields, and any control whose locator a form tool already uses. Do not edit scanner.py or store.py.
work_items.acceptance: A new test fails before the fix and passes after. A page with no <form> and a lone `<input type=search placeholder='Search products'>` whose Enter handler writes the query into #out yields a 'search' tool with a required 'query'. Calling it with 'lamp' makes #out show 'lamp'. A form-less checkbox does not produce an extra search tool. All of test_site_synthesis.py still passes, including test_page_content_does_not_become_tools and test_a_bare_search_input_is_still_recognised_as_search.

work_items.title: Scroll-independent fingerprint, covering form-less controls, plus the single SYNTHESIS_VERSION bump
work_items.problem: byRelevance (scanner.py:216-229) picks which items survive the MAX_BUTTONS and MAX_CONTROLS caps by their position in the viewport. fingerprint() (store.py:41-61) hashes the surviving names, so on a large page scrolling changes the fingerprint. The cached manifest, including its verified flags, is then discarded, and store.put overwrites the persisted one. Separately, fingerprint() ignores `controls` altogether, so renaming a form-less search box (which FIX-2 turns into a tool) never invalidates the cache.
work_items.approach: In SCAN_JS, also return a `shape` summary built from the full candidate lists in document order, taken before the cap and bounded by the existing slice limits: names of buttonCandidates, looseCandidates and each form's controls. Leave the capped, viewport-ranked lists unchanged. In fingerprint(), when `affordances.get('shape')` is a dict, hash that together with views/toggles/tables/pagers. Otherwise keep the current behaviour. Include form-less control names in the hash either way. Bump SYNTHESIS_VERSION from 2 to 3. Do not touch service.py.
work_items.acceptance: A new test fails before the fix and passes after. On a tall page with more than 25 named buttons at the top and more than 25 different named buttons far below, fingerprint(scan) is the same before and after scrolling to the bottom, while the capped `buttons` list differs between the two scans. work_items.title: WebMCP call_tool runs a stale synthesized tool instead of the page's own declared tool
work_items.problem: call_tool (service.py:247-257) looks up the per-origin synthesized manifest first and runs any synthesized tool whose name matches, without checking what the latest discovery lists for this target. If a page first gets a synthesized 'search' and later declares its own 'search' (an SPA registering after load, or a same-origin navigation), call_tool still drives the old UI steps. That breaks the module's rule that a real declaration always wins.
work_items.approach: Take the synthesized path only when `self._cache.get(cdp_session.target_id)` lists the name with source == 'synthesized'. Otherwise fall through to the bridge call. Keep the existing error/ok mapping and the verified update, and pass cdp_session.target_id to synthesizer.call. Do not change discover().
work_items.acceptance: A new test fails before the fix and passes after, on BrowserProfile(enable_webmcp=True). A page has a search form and, about 1s after load, registers a declared 'search' tool returning 'declared:'+q. Discover once (synthesized), wait, discover again (declared js 'search' is listed), then call_tool('search', {'q':'x'}). The result content is 'declared:x' and the form was not used. test_webmcp.py and test_site_synthesis.py still pass.
work_items.test_idea: Serve the page with pytest-httpserver; the form's onsubmit sets window.__formUsed=true so the test can check the synthesized path did not run. Use the webmcp_session fixture pattern from test_site_synthesis.py.

work_items.title: Human input: a cancelled hold, press_and_hold, click or keystroke leaves the key or mouse button stuck down
work_items.problem: hold, press_and_hold, click, press and type_text all await a sleep between the down event and the up event, with no try/finally. Agent step timeouts cancel tasks in the middle of those sleeps. When that happens the keyUp or mouseReleased is never sent, so the page and Blink keep the key or button held.
work_items.approach: Wrap each down…up pair in try/finally and send the matching release (same params) in the finally. Guard that send with try/except Exception plus logger.debug so a dead session or a second cancel cannot mask the original exception. Never swallow CancelledError. Keep timing and jitter unchanged.
work_items.acceptance: New tests fail before the fix and pass after. (1) Cancel a hold('ArrowRight', 5) task after about 0.4s: it raises CancelledError and the last logged ArrowRight event is keyup. (2) Cancel press_and_hold over a box the same way: the last event is mouseup. tests/ci/test_human_input.py still passes.
work_items.test_idea: pytest-httpserver page that pushes keydown/keyup and mousedown/mouseup events into window.__log. Read it with run_page_script after a short sleep.

work_items.title: Cobrowse: launch_for_human leaks the Chrome process (and its profile lock) when the debugging port never comes up
work_items.problem: launch_for_human (service.py:165-167) spawns Chrome and then awaits _wait_for_cdp with no cleanup path. On a TimeoutError, CancelledError or KeyError, the process is orphaned and keeps the persistent profile locked. HumanBrowser.close() also kills the process without awaiting wait(), which leaves a zombie, and does not guard against ProcessLookupError.
work_items.approach: Add a `_terminate(process)` helper: terminate, wait a few seconds, kill if still running, then await wait(), guarding ProcessLookupError. Call it from a BaseException handler around _wait_for_cdp before re-raising, and reuse it in HumanBrowser.close()'s fallback. Add a `launch_timeout: float = LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_S` parameter and pass it through to _wait_for_cdp. Default behaviour is unchanged.
work_items.acceptance: A new test fails before the fix and passes after. launch_for_human with executable_path pointing at a shell script that runs `exec sleep 30`, called with launch_timeout=1.5, raises TimeoutError and leaves no 'sleep' child process (checked with psutil). test_cobrowse.py still passes.
work_items.test_idea: The fake browser is a real executable script written into tmp_path; list children with psutil.Process().children(recursive=True). No mocking.

work_items.title: Decide: parse_decisions raises on a malformed usage block (breaks the never-raises contract), and choose_tool can return a tool it never offered
work_items.problem: ask() is documented as 'Never raises', but parse_decisions runs outside its try block. service.py:125-126 calls int() on usage values from the response, which raises ValueError, OverflowError or TypeError on values like 'n/a', 1e400 or [1]. Separately, choose_tool (page.py:235-241) returns any confident answer without checking that it is one of the offered tool names.
work_items.approach: Add a `_count(value) -> int` helper that returns 0 for anything that is not a finite, non-negative, non-bool number. As a backstop, wrap the parse_decisions call in ask() so an unexpected parse error is logged at debug and returns Decisions(). Keep the ValueError for too many questions, which is deliberate. Drop non-finite confidence values. In choose_tool, return None when answer.value is not among the offered names.
work_items.acceptance: New tests fail before the fix and pass after. (1) A response with usage {'input_tokens':'n/a','output_tokens':1e400} does not make ask() raise. (2) An answer of 'not_offered' at confidence 0.99 makes choose_tool return None. test_decide.py still passes.
work_items.test_idea: Reuse the jev_server pytest-httpserver fixture pattern from tests/ci/test_decide.py; build a WebMCPPageTools with two tools for choose_tool.

work_items.title: WebMCP bridge: the manifest deadline does not bound in-flight fetches (discovery can hang indefinitely), and window.agent is installed despite the stated policy
work_items.problem: (a) LIMITS.manifestMs is checked only between manifest refs. The manifest fetch has no AbortSignal and the tools/list rpc uses the full rpcMs, so a manifest server that never responds leaves the shared inFlightDiscovery promise pending forever. bridge.call() for any unknown name then hangs as well. (b) bridge.py:375 installs window.agent, directly contradicting the comment at line 370, and gives anti-bot scripts a free fingerprint.
work_items.approach: (a) Create one AbortController per loadManifests pass, abort it at manifestMs, and clear the timer in a finally. Pass its signal to the manifest fetch and the json() read. Let rpc() take an optional outer signal so tools/list during loading is bounded by the same deadline. On abort, record 'manifest loading timed out' and return what was found. (b) Remove the install(window, 'agent', …) line.
work_items.acceptance: New tests fail before the fix and pass after. (1) With a hanging /hang manifest and a JS-registered tool 'ping', call_tool('missing_tool') returns 'no WebMCP tool named' within about 8s, and a later discovery lists 'ping'. (2) typeof window.agent is 'undefined' while navigator.modelContext exists. test_webmcp.py and test_browser_fingerprint.py still pass.
work_items.test_idea: Use a pytest-httpserver handler that time.sleep()s for the manifest, on a threaded server if supported; time the call with time.monotonic(). Session: BrowserProfile(headless=True, enable_webmcp=True).

work_items.title: Profile (lower priority): the headless 'headful' user agent always claims Linux, contradicting navigator.platform on macOS/Windows
work_items.problem: _headful_user_agent (profile.py:1010) hardcodes 'X11; Linux x86_64' on every host. On macOS and Windows headless sessions, the UA contradicts navigator.platform and userAgentData, which is itself an automation signal.
work_items.approach: Add a pure `_ua_os_token(system: str) -> str` helper: Darwin maps to 'Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7', Windows maps to 'Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64', anything else to 'X11; Linux x86_64'. Use it with platform.system(). Change nothing else.

result.summary:
FIX-2 confirmed and fixed: `SiteToolSynthesizer.synthesize()` never read `affordances['controls']`, so the scanner's loose-control list — collected precisely because "a site-wide search box usually lives here" — was scanned, ranked, budgeted and then discarded. A standalone `<input type=search>` wired to a JS keydown handler (the normal SPA search box, no `<form>` anywhere) produced no tool at all, even though `ToolStep.key` exists for exactly that Enter press.

Changes, all in `browser_use/synthesis/service.py`:

1. Extracted the search test out of `_tool_from_form` into a shared static helper `_looks_like_search(label, roles, types, keys)`. Semantics are byte-for-byte the same as the inlined version (verified against the four form shapes in the existing suite: bare `q` → `search(query: string)`, shop search → `search(query: string)`, login → `sign_in(email: string)`, filter → `apply_filter(size?: string)` — all identical to before the refactor). The two paths now cannot drift.
2. Added `_is_text_entry(control)`: role `textbox`/`searchbox`, or `combobox` with no `options`. A native `<select>` also reports `combobox` but arrives carrying its options and has to be driven through the DOM; an ARIA combobox with no options is a typeahead search box. Checkboxes, radios and buttons fall out here.
3. Added `_tool_from_control(control, used)`: rejects sensitive fields and non-text-entry controls, then requires `_looks_like_search`. Produces `self._unique('search', used)` with a required string `query` and steps `[fill(locator, param='query'), press(locator, key='Enter')]`.
4. Added the loop in `synthesize()` immediately after the forms loop, under the `MAX_TOOLS_PER_SITE` guard, skipping any control whose locator a form tool already drives (compared via `Locator.model_dump_json()`). That guard is not redundant: the scanner's `!el.closest('form')` filter does not pierce shadow boundaries upward, so an input in a shadow root inside a light-DOM `<form>` really does appear in both lists.

`scanner.py` and `store.py` untouched. Ruff check and format both clean.

Two adjacent problems I did NOT touch because the brief forbade editing store.py — worth a decision at integration:
- `SYNTHESIS_VERSION` is still 2. Its whole stated purpose is "bumped whenever a change to synthesis would produce a different tool from the same page", which is exactly what this change does. Without a bump to 3, a user with an existing on-disk cache for a form-less-search site keeps being served the old search-less manifest indefinitely, since the page fingerprint has not changed.
- `store.fingerprint()` hashes forms, buttons, views, toggles, tables and pagers — but not `controls`. Now that loose controls yield tools, two pages on one origin that differ only in their loose search box hash identically, so the second is served the first's surface. Pre-existing, but this change is what makes it bite.

+"""A search box that belongs to no <form> — which is how most of the modern web ships it.
+
+The scanner has always collected visible controls outside any form and reported them as
+`controls`, on the reasoning that "a site-wide search box usually lives here". Synthesis
+never read that list, so the single commonest affordance on the web went missing on every
+site that wires its search box to a keydown handler instead of a form submit. The page
+below is exactly that shape: one `<input type=search>`, no form, Enter handled in JS.

+

+
+import pytest
+from pytest_httpserver import HTTPServer
+
+from browser_use.browser.events import NavigateToUrlEvent
+from browser_use.synthesis import SiteToolSynthesizer
+
+# No <form> anywhere. The checkbox is deliberately labelled with a search word: it must be
+# rejected for being a checkbox, not for what it happens to be called.
+SPA_PAGE = """<!DOCTYPE html>
+<html><head><title>SPA Shop</title></head><body>
+	<input type="search" placeholder="Search products" id="s">
+	<input type="checkbox" id="stock" aria-label="Find in stock only">
+	<div id="out">idle</div>
+<script>
+	s.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'Enter') out.textContent = s.value; });
+</script>
+</body></html>"""
+
+# A loose text field that is nothing to do with search. Pressing Enter in it is a guess,
+# so it must not become a tool.
+PLAIN_PAGE = """<!DOCTYPE html>
+<html><head><title>Notes</title></head><body>
+	<input type="text" aria-label="Nickname" id="nick">
+	<input type="password" aria-label="Search vault" id="pw">
+</body></html>"""
+
+

+	server = HTTPServer()

+	server.expect_request('/plain').respond_with_data(PLAIN_PAGE, content_type='text/html')

+

+	event = session.event_bus.dispatch(NavigateToUrlEvent(url=url))

+

Confirmed bug and fixed it. In `browser_use/human/input.py` every down/up pair (`click`, `type_text`, `press`, `hold`, `press_and_hold`) awaited a sleep between the down event and the up event with no cleanup. An agent step timeout cancels the task mid-sleep — which is where nearly all the wall time in those methods lives — so `CancelledError` is thrown at the sleep, the coroutine unwinds, and the matching `keyUp`/`mouseReleased` is never dispatched. The Python task dies but the renderer never hears about it: Blink and the page keep the key or button held, so the next action types into a browser still holding ArrowRight, or drags instead of clicking, with nothing in the logs explaining it.

Fix: each down…up pair is now `try: <sleep> finally: await self._release(...)`, with the release sent using exactly the same params as before. `_release` is a new static helper that awaits the send, re-raises `asyncio.CancelledError` unchanged (swallowing it would make these methods uncancellable), and catches only `Exception` into a `logger.debug` — so a dead CDP session or a navigated-away page cannot replace the exception already propagating. Timing, jitter, auto-repeat cadence and the normal-path event order are untouched; the release simply moved into the `finally` that already runs on the happy path.

Note on scope: `move_to` and `wheel` are unchanged — neither leaves state latched in the renderer when interrupted, so wrapping them would add noise without fixing anything.

Regression test `tests/ci/test_human_input_cancellation.py` serves a pytest-httpserver page that records every keydown/keyup/mousedown/mouseup into `window.__log` and reads it back with `run_page_script`:
1. `hold('ArrowRight', 5)` cancelled ~0.4s in — raises `CancelledError`, last ArrowRight event must be `keyup`. Fails before the fix (last event is an auto-repeat `keydown`).
2. `press_and_hold(box, 5)` cancelled the same way — last button0 event must be `mouseup`. Fails before the fix (no `mouseup` at all).
3. An uncancelled `hold('ArrowLeft', 0.3)` still ends in exactly one `keyup` and still auto-repeats, guarding against the cleanup path double-releasing or displacing the happy path.

Both cancellation tests wait for the page to actually observe the down event before cancelling, so a slow CDP round trip during pointer travel cannot make the test pass for the wrong reason. No virtualenv here, so the suite was not run — `tests/ci/test_human_input.py` is untouched and its normal-path event sequences are unchanged by construction.

FIX-7 confirmed as a real bug on both counts and fixed.

(1) `Jev.ask()` is documented "Never raises", but `parse_decisions` ran outside the try block and did `int(usage.get('input_tokens') or 0)` on whatever the server sent. Verified the three raising paths concretely: `int('n/a')` -> ValueError, `int(json.loads('1e400'))` -> OverflowError (JSON 1e400 decodes to float inf), `int([1])` -> TypeError. So a 200 OK with a junk usage block took down the agent step the decision model was supposed to be optimizing — exactly the dependency the module docstring swears it is not.

Fix: added `_count(value) -> int` which returns 0 for bools, non-numbers, negatives and non-finite floats. It checks `isinstance(value, int)` before touching `math.isfinite`, because `math.isfinite(10**400)` itself raises OverflowError (it coerces to float) — a large JSON integer is a legitimate finite count and is passed through. Added a backstop `try/except Exception` around the `parse_decisions` call in `ask()`, logging at debug and returning `Decisions()`. The deliberate `ValueError` for >MAX_QUESTIONS is untouched — it fires before the request and stays.

Also added `_finite(value) -> float | None` for confidence: inf clears every threshold and nan clears none, so `Answer.certain()` would have been reporting a verdict the model never gave. bools are rejected too (`True` previously became confidence 1.0, i.e. instantly certain). `float()` is wrapped for the huge-int OverflowError case.

(2) `choose_tool` returned any sufficiently confident answer without checking it against the options it offered. A choice is only meaningful over its own criteria set; a name outside it is a hallucinated tool that fails at call time. Added `if answer.value not in options: return None`, placed after the NO_TOOL check and before the certainty check so the debug log lines stay distinct. `options` is built from `page_tools.tools[:MAX_CHOICE_OPTIONS - 1]`, so a tool truncated out of the offer is also correctly rejected.
